answer: Trust propagates from authenticated seeds through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, with voting mass conserved and capped per seed. A Sybil cluster connected to honest nodes by a sparse cut has low conductance, so few walks cross its bridge; min-cut and transitivity bounds then limit its aggregate voting weight to the incoming trusted mass, not the internal tide of fabricated identities. A lantern-like seed cannot confer unbounded weight by repeated attestations.
